OUTPATIENT PHYSICAL THERAPY NOTE
Date of Service: 2026-04-20
Patient: Robert Nguyen | DOB: 1955-11-02 | MRN: 00198734
Clinician: Dr. Mark Torres, PT, DPT, OCS
Visit Type: Initial Evaluation

CHIEF COMPLAINT:
Patient presents with right knee pain rated 7/10 on the Numeric Pain Rating Scale (NPRS),
described as deep, aching, and constant, with sharp exacerbations during stair negotiation
and prolonged standing. Patient reports morning stiffness lasting approximately 30 minutes.

DIAGNOSIS:
Right knee osteoarthritis — ICD-10: M17.11 (Primary osteoarthritis, right knee)

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS:
Mr. Nguyen is a 70-year-old retired postal worker with a 4-year history of progressive right
knee pain. Symptoms have worsened over the past 6 months to the point of functional
limitation. He was evaluated by orthopedics 3 weeks ago; X-ray confirmed moderate-to-severe
joint space narrowing at the medial compartment with osteophyte formation. Orthopedist
deferred surgical intervention and referred to physical therapy for conservative management.
Prior treatment: NSAIDs (naproxen 500 mg BID) with partial relief, cortisone injection
6 months ago with temporary improvement (approximately 8 weeks). No prior physical therapy
for this condition. Patient reports activity-limiting pain with walking >1 block,
ascending/descending stairs, and rising from a chair.

OBJECTIVE FINDINGS:
- Right knee ROM: flexion 95° (limited, nl 135°), extension -8° (flexion contracture, nl 0°)
- Left knee ROM: flexion 128°, extension 0° (within normal limits)
- Strength testing (right): quadriceps 3+/5, hamstrings 4/5, hip abductors 4-/5
- Strength testing (left): quadriceps 4+/5, hamstrings 4+/5
- Special tests: positive patellar grind, positive valgus stress test (medial laxity grade I)
- Palpation: tenderness at medial joint line and patellar tendon insertion
- Gait: antalgic gait pattern right, decreased right stance phase, Trendelenburg sign noted
- Functional: 30-second sit-to-stand test: 6 repetitions (norm for age/sex: ≥12)
- Edema: 1+ pitting edema circumferentially at right knee

FUNCTIONAL LIMITATIONS:
Patient is unable to walk more than one city block without rest secondary to pain and fatigue.
He is unable to climb stairs without use of a railing and reports only 1 flight maximum.
Unable to rise from a standard chair without upper extremity assist. Patient is retired but
reports inability to perform yard work, grocery shopping, and recreational walking with spouse.
Patient lives in a two-story home; bedroom is upstairs.

TREATMENT PROVIDED TODAY (75 minutes):
1. Therapeutic exercise — quad sets, straight leg raises, short arc quads, terminal knee
   extension with band; 3 sets x 15 reps each (20 min)
2. Manual therapy — patellar mobilization (inferior and medial glides, grades III-IV),
   tibiofemoral joint mobilization grades II-III (15 min)
3. Neuromuscular re-education — weight-shifting, single-leg stance progression,
   step-up training 4-inch step (15 min)
4. Therapeutic activities — sit-to-stand training, stair negotiation practice (10 min)
5. Cryotherapy — ice pack to right knee post-exercise (15 min)

RESPONSE TO TREATMENT:
Patient tolerated treatment well with mild post-exercise soreness. NPRS improved from 7/10
to 5/10 by end of session. Patient demonstrated improved sit-to-stand mechanics with verbal
and tactile cueing. Right knee flexion improved to 100° following joint mobilization.

ASSESSMENT:
Patient presents with significant functional deficits consistent with moderate-to-severe knee
osteoarthritis. Prognosis for functional improvement with skilled PT is fair given severity of
structural changes, however meaningful gains in strength, ROM, and functional mobility are
anticipated with consistent participation. Patient is motivated and engaged.

PLAN:
Plan of care: 3x/week for 6 weeks (18 visits total).
Short-term goals (3 weeks): Right knee flexion to 110°, quadriceps strength 4/5,
  sit-to-stand ≥10 reps in 30 seconds, ambulation 3 blocks without rest, NPRS ≤4/10.
Long-term goals (6 weeks): Right knee flexion to 120°, independent home exercise program,
  stair negotiation without railing assist, NPRS ≤2/10 with functional activities.
HEP: Patient educated on quad sets and straight leg raises to perform 2x daily.
  Demonstrated correct technique; verbalized understanding.
Coordination: Orthopedic follow-up in 6 weeks to reassess surgical candidacy based on
  response to PT.
